Of all the tickets printed for "Diamond Bingo", about two-thirds are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with five of seven top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "Diamond Bingo" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
804.headline: How much has sold

805.body:
"Multiply Your Money" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

If "Multiply Your Money" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
805.headline: Tickets sold so far

806.body:
"Win $50, $100 or $200" has 166,284 prizes of $50 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100 prize, with 56,594 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "Win $50, $100 or $200" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
806.headline: The prize table, line by line

807.body:
One of Ravens X2's top prizes was claimed last week. A player in Maryland won $20,000. The game started with four top prizes and now has two top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Today's free summary of "Ravens X2" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
807.headline: A top prize was just claimed

808.body:
The most common win left on "Ravens X10" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "Ravens X10" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
808.headline: What the prize table shows

809.body:
On "Gold Bar Bingo", one $50,000 top prize was claimed in this morning's update. That leaves five of the original seven. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Tomorrow's count on "Gold Bar Bingo" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
809.headline: The top prize list got shorter

810.body:
One of In the Green's top prizes was claimed four days ago. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with seven top prizes and now has five top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

The table below shows the full count for "In the Green", with every prize level included.
810.headline: Top prize count went down

811.body:
"Extreme Green" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The numbers for "Extreme Green" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
811.headline: The prize mix in this game

812.body:
"Loose Change®" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $1,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold fifteen of the original 24. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Every line of Loose Change®'s prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
812.headline: Someone claimed a $1,000 prize

813.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "The Price is Right™", about two-thirds are still unsold. The game is in the middle of its run, with four of six top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "The Price is Right™" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
813.headline: Early stage or late

814.body:
"High Voltage" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $100,000 was claimed four days ago. Unsold tickets still hold six of the original eight. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "High Voltage" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
814.headline: A player won a top prize

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" has gone two weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a quarter of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $100,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$100,000 Crossword" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
815.headline: Top prizes are still left

816.body:
"Deluxe Crossword" is still new, with most of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "Deluxe Crossword" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
816.headline: How far along this game is

817.body:
A $50,000 top prize on "Hello Money!" was claimed last week. The game started with seven top prizes and has six top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "Hello Money!" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
817.headline: A top prize was just claimed

818.body:
10X Cash's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $1,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Every line of 10X Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
818.headline: The prize mix in this game

819.body:
"30X Cash" offers a top prize of $30,000 and eight prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The numbers for "30X Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
819.headline: Where the prize money is

820.body:
"Cozy Cash" just reached Maryland stores with 35 top prizes of $500. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

If you play "Cozy Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
820.headline: A new game is here

821.body:
"Season's Greetings" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $2 game with six top prizes of $10,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The numbers for "Season's Greetings" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
821.headline: Brand new, no claims yet

822.body:
"Peppermint Payout" has joined the Maryland lineup at $3 with six top prizes of $30,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Every line of Peppermint Payout's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
822.headline: Brand new, no claims yet

823.body:
"Holly-Day Cash" just reached Maryland stores with seven top prizes of $50,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Everything above about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
823.headline: New in stores

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" just went on sale in Maryland. The game has ten full prize levels with nine top prizes of $100,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

Today's free summary of "Winter Multiplier" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
824.headline: New game, all prizes left

825.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Win $100, $200 or $500", nearly all are still unsold. The game is still new, with 12,635 of 12,822 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Tomorrow's count on "Win $100, $200 or $500" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
